title: Biology 2e 28.4 Superphylum Lophotrochozoa: Mollusks and Annelids
text: The annelids and the mollusks are the most familiar of the lophotrochozoan protostomes. They are also more “typical” lophotrochozoans, since both groups include aquatic species with trochophore larvae, which unite both taxa in common ancestry. These phyla show how a flexible body plan can lead to biological success in terms of abundance and species diversity. The phylum Mollusca has the second greatest number of species of all animal phyla with nearly 100,000 described extant species, and about 80,000 described extinct species. In fact, it is estimated that about 25 percent of all known marine species are mollusks! The annelids and mollusks are both bilaterally symmetrical, cephalized, triploblastic, schizocoelous eucoelomates They include animals you are likely to see in your backyard or on your dinner plate!
